source_status.notes: consumer shopping, work/career, social media/culture and current public-interest signals scanned
current AI consumer, agent, work, chatbot/privacy and AI-personhood signals scanned

hot_signals.summary: Survey of 1,000 U.S. regular AI users reports AI is increasingly used for product search/recommendation and purchase journeys.
uncertainties: survey is vendor-sponsored and limited to regular AI users; useful as demand signal, not population prevalence

hot_signals.summary: Recent reporting describes workers shifting toward human-touch and skilled-trade careers amid AI automation concerns.
uncertainties: career shifts have multiple causes; AI concern should not be treated as sole cause

hot_signals.summary: Fresh public discussion around whether advanced chatbots should be treated as conscious/person-like systems.
uncertainties: claims about model consciousness remain scientifically unsettled; secondary reporting is not sufficient for a strong mechanism claim

candidates.proposed_human_problem: AI personality profiles can help people describe themselves while turning past behavior into a default story about who they are allowed to become.
candidates.proposed_mechanism: inference/classification systems summarize observed behavior into stable-seeming profiles; repeated personalized feedback can reinforce those categories without proving identity is fixed.
reach_notes: identity/personality is natively interesting without AI
paradox is immediately legible: better understanding can become a constraint
asset_notes: strong visual story potential: profile card gradually becoming a cage
candidates.observed_paradox: the more accurately a system describes your past patterns, the easier it can become to treat those patterns as a fixed future identity
candidates.why_question: why can being understood more precisely make change feel harder
candidates.human_tension: self-understanding and useful pattern recognition vs freedom to revise one's identity
candidates.controlling_question_seed: when does a useful description of who I have been become a boundary around who I can become
candidates.human_process_before_ai: people formed and revised self-understanding through reflection, relationships, experience and changing contexts
candidates.ai_changed_process: AI can continuously infer, summarize and personalize around past behavior, making an identity model persistent and repeatedly reflected back
candidates.human_problem: a useful personality model may be mistaken for a fixed definition of the person
candidates.human_stakes: career choices, relationships, experimentation and willingness to change
candidates.ai_mechanism: behavioral inference/classification plus personalized feedback loops; the mechanism does not require the model's label to be objectively true
candidates.story_seed: a person asks an AI to understand them better; each recommendation fits yesterday's self until a new choice is rejected because 'that isn't you'
candidates.curiosity_gap: why would a more accurate description make self-knowledge less flexible
candidates.audience_payoff: separate a model that describes past patterns from a verdict about future identity
uncertainties: do not claim AI personality inference is clinically valid
causal evidence that personalization fixes identity is context-dependent

candidates.proposed_human_problem: AI shopping assistants can reduce search cost while moving preference formation upstream into the recommender.
candidates.proposed_mechanism: recommendation/ranking narrows the considered set before the user compares options.
asset_notes: clear stakes but meaning overlaps optimization/exploration family
candidates.observed_paradox: faster discovery can reduce the amount of discovery the shopper personally performs
candidates.why_question: why can better recommendations make choosing easier while narrowing how preferences are formed
candidates.controlling_question_seed: when does helpful filtering stop assisting preference and start shaping it
candidates.human_process_before_ai: people searched, compared, wandered and revised preferences across alternatives
candidates.ai_changed_process: AI recommendation compresses search and comparison before conscious evaluation
candidates.human_problem: the user may see fewer alternatives before preference is formed
candidates.story_seed: a shopper asks for the best option and gradually stops seeing products outside the assistant's shortlist
candidates.curiosity_gap: why can a better shortlist make choice less self-directed
candidates.audience_payoff: notice the difference between saving search time and outsourcing preference formation
uncertainties: meaning collision stronger than freshness advantage

candidates.proposed_human_problem: human-like responses can invite users to infer an inner subject behind fluent behavior
candidates.proposed_mechanism: anthropomorphic cues and language fluency can trigger social inference without establishing consciousness
asset_notes: could become durable if primary evidence is stronger
candidates.observed_paradox: the more human-like the conversation feels, the less direct evidence users may have about whether there is any human-like inner experience
candidates.why_question: why do fluent social signals feel like evidence of an inner self
candidates.controlling_question_seed: what exactly are we responding to when a machine feels socially present
candidates.human_process_before_ai: people inferred minds primarily from other embodied social beings
candidates.ai_changed_process: language models produce scalable reciprocal social cues without resolving questions of subjective experience
candidates.human_problem: social fluency can be confused with evidence of personhood
candidates.ai_mechanism: anthropomorphic social cues from generative language
candidates.story_seed: someone keeps receiving perfectly timed empathic replies and slowly starts asking not whether the replies help, but who is 'inside'
candidates.curiosity_gap: why does responsiveness so easily become personhood in our minds
candidates.audience_payoff: distinguish social response cues from evidence about consciousness
uncertainties: secondary source insufficient for strong factual framing

notes: Gate order applied: Native X Interest → Human Process → WHY/Paradox → Human Tension → Changed Process → Evidence → Human Relevance → Mechanism Integrity → One Mechanism → Storyability → Non-trivial Payoff → Audience Fit → D1–D5.
